[09:12:04] user: Add refresh-token rotation. Requirements: every refresh must
issue a new token AND revoke the previous one; rotation must be atomic; the
existing /login contract must not change; add tests.

[09:13:20] assistant: Starting with auth/tokens.py. I'll add `rotate_token`
which mints a new token and marks the old one revoked.

[09:19:41] assistant: Tried doing the revoke inside the same DB transaction as
the mint. Our session store is Redis, not Postgres, so there's no transaction
to join. Rejected that approach.

[09:22:03] assistant: Second attempt: Redis MULTI/EXEC pipeline. That works for
atomicity within Redis, so going with it.

[09:31:15] assistant: Assumption: the Redis client here is the sync one and
MULTI/EXEC is actually atomic under our connection pool. I have not verified
the pool doesn't hand the two commands to different connections.

[09:38:52] assistant: `validate_token` in auth/session.py is now partly
redundant. Leaving it for now - the callers in api/routes.py still use it.

[09:44:10] assistant: Tests: 11 pass, 1 fails -
test_rotation_revokes_old_token. The old token still validates after rotation.
I believe this is a test fixture issue rather than a real bug, but I have not
confirmed that.

[09:46:33] assistant: Checkpointing here. Rotation is implemented; the revoke
half is not proven to work.
